This appeal has been filed by the claimant/appellant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 09.11.2021 passed in MACC.No.100002/2015 by 3rd Additional M.A.C.T., Sihora District- Jabalpur seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to para-18 and 19 of impugned award, submits that Tribunal has wrongly determined permanent disability as 7%, whereas, as per medical evidence, appellant suffered 20% permanent disability.
It is also urged that permanent disability suffered by the appellant would also adversely affect marriage prospects of appellant.
It is also urged that Tribunal has awarded lower amount under other head also.
Therefore, compensation awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.

4. Learned counsel for respondent No.3/Insurance Company submits that Tribunal has awarded appropriate compensation following law laid down in Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited AIR (2014) 12 SCC 396.

entities.text: Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited AIR (2014) 12 SCC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, no enhancement is required.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2/owner submits that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
No enhancement is required.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.

7. Perusal of impugned award reveals that in para-19, Tribunal has held that appellant suffered 7 %
permanent disability and in para-35, after relying upon Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager,
National Insurance Company Lim ited reported in AIR (2014) 12 SCC 396, awarded Rs.1,00,000/-
as compensation.

entities.text:
Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager,
National Insurance Company Lim ited reported in AIR (2014) 12 SCC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Tribunal also awarded Rs.15,000/- for conveyance/attendant charges/nourishing diet, Rs.15,000/- for pain and suffering and Rs.11,277/- for medical expenses.

8. So far as percentage of permanent disability is concerned, Dr. Sharadchandra Dwivedi has admitted in his cross-examination that 20% permanent disability assessed by him is with respect to right leg only and he has also deposed in his cross-examination that he has assessed 10% permanent disability with respect to malunion of bone of right knee and 10% for Epiphysis.
Hence, in view of above, in this Court's opinion, it would be proper to determine disability 10% in relation to whole body.

9. So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, this issue stands concluded by Hon'ble Apex Court in Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited reported in AIR (2014) 12 SCC 396.

entities.text: Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited reported in AIR (2014) 12 SCC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In para-12, Hon'ble Apex Court has held as under:-
"12.

Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts,
we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc. should be, if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body, Rs 3 lakhs; up to 60%, Rs 4 lakhs; up to 90%, Rs 5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs 6 lakhs.

For permanent disability up Ku. Shivani Kumhar (Minor) vs Neeraj Lodhi on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8379142/
2 to 10%, it should be Rs 1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick."
10.

entities.text: Ku. Shivani Kumhar (Minor) vs Neeraj Lodhi on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in para-12 of Mallikarjun (Supra),
compensation is to be awarded as per percentage of permanent disablement and further, it will include all other heads except actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc.
11.
As in the instant case, appellant has suffered 10% permanent disability.
Therefore, in view of Mallikarjun (Supra), appellant is entitled to receive Rs.1,00,000/- for permanent disability as awarded by the Tribunal.
Further, Tribunal has also awarded medical expenses etc.
There is nothing on record to show that amount awarded by Tribunal under other heads (medical expenses, attendant charges etc.) has not been awarded as per documents available on record.
12. Hence, in view of above, no enhancement is required in compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation relying upon Mallikarjun (Supra).
13.
Hence, appeal filed by appellant is dismissed.
